## 3. A stiffness-free loss clock, acquired from a finite matrix

Define the stacked physical jump operator Jcal=column_mu L_mu and the scalar

    f(t)^2=||E^dagger F(t)||_F^2,
    J(t)=integral_0^t f(s)^2 ds
        =tr[I-F(t)^dagger F(t)] <= M.

The last equality follows by differentiating tr(F^dagger F). It is a trace over the M one-particle modes, not the exponentially large Fock space.

The exact intertwining identity

    a(v)Gamma(F)=Gamma(F)a(vF)

gives, on N<=K,

    ||Jcal B(t)|| <= sqrt(K) f(t).

It also constructs this normalized jump block. For v_mu(t)=e_mu^dagger F(t), prepare the color state with amplitudes ||v_mu||/f; rotate v_mu/||v_mu|| to one mode; block-encode its annihilator by amplitude sqrt(n/K) and a reversible decrement; rotate back; then apply Gamma(F) on the remaining particles. The output color is retained. This gives Jcal B(t)/(sqrt(K)f(t)) without a normalization proportional to ||E||. Zero or negligible components are zero-selected with an absolute allocated error, never resampled conditionally.

This is the load-bearing structural bound. Replacing f by ||E|| would reintroduce stiffness; taking a trace over the full Fock dimension would introduce an exponential memory cost.

and the right probabilities are2^-B. For a binary prefix specifying an interval[a,b], its exact mass is [J(b)-J(a)]/J(t). Compute these masses reversibly from the M-by-M matrix exponential, then use the two child masses to perform a controlled rotation. One conditional arithmetic computation per level prepares the whole amplitude state; it does NOT enumerate2^B leaves. The outer source uses the equally explicit cumulative mass W(t)=2KJ(t)+16Kv^2Mt^2 and its interval differences. Color distributions use explicit finite vector norms. ## CDF preparation, tiny prefixes and division

For either cumulative distribution `J` or `W`, one reversible finite-matrix evaluation supplies the mass of any addressed dyadic interval. At depth `b`, prepare the next bit by the normalized masses of its two child intervals. Thus a `B`-bit clock uses `B` coherent prefix evaluations and finite rotations, rather than a list of `2^B` probabilities.

If a prefix has total probability below `xi=eta^2/(100 B 2^B)`, choose any conditional rotation there. There are at most `2^B` prefixes at a given depth, so the sum of affected probabilities is at most `eta^2/(100B)` at that depth. For the state-error bound, select only the **first** such prefix on each path. These selected subtrees are disjoint; their ancestor rotations are unchanged. The squared difference between the two states within a subtree is at most four times its original mass. Summing the disjoint masses over depths therefore gives a squared state error `O(eta^2)`, without a triangle-inequality loss of `sqrt(B)`. On the remaining prefixes, compute masses with absolute error `O(xi eta^2/B^2)` and rotation angles to `O(eta/B)`. Division then has an explicitly positive denominator at least a constant times `xi`. Its bit length is `O(B+log(B/eta))`. Certified absolute mass errors distinguish masses above `2xi` from those below `xi`; changing the threshold by a constant covers the indeterminate strip. Clip negative finite errors and normalize each two-child vector before rotating; this always prepares an actual normalized state. The rotation-synthesis errors are added in ordinary circuit norm over the `B` levels. These operations hold uniformly over a coherent duration.

For the normalized loss direction, the convolution is omitted when `J(t)<=M eta^2`: its already explicit multiplier `sqrt(J/M)` makes the signal error at most `eta`.
